capabilities: Snapshot the vault to Dropbox on a configurable schedule (incremental and full)
Browse snapshots and restore individual files or whole versions from a Backup Browser
Prune old backups automatically with hierarchical retention tiers and garbage collection
Recover snapshots without Obsidian using a bundled standalone Node restore CLI
Store Dropbox OAuth tokens in Obsidian's encrypted secret store
disambiguation: Despite the name, it does not archive or organize notes; its only job is backing the vault up to Dropbox and restoring from those backups.
extras: Backups are stored as content-addressed blobs plus manifests, not a 1:1 vault mirror, so files cannot be grabbed directly from the Dropbox web interface. Dropbox will show an 'app not yet verified' warning during OAuth. On Linux without a keyring, token storage falls back to obfuscation rather than real encryption. Detailed documentation lives in a docs/ folder referenced from the README.
intentEvidence: If you decide to switch from Aut-O-Backups to Archivist:
problem: Obsidian has no built-in offsite backup with per-file version history, so an accidental delete or overwrite can permanently lose work unless the user set up external backups.

relations.evidence: There's another Obsidian community plugin that also backs up to Dropbox: Aut-O-Backups

requires.name: Dropbox desktop sync (for standalone CLI break-glass recovery)

summary: Backup plugin that schedules versioned vault snapshots to Dropbox with content-addressed storage, hierarchical retention, and per-file restore.
